bearerAuth.description: API key from the dashboard. `isnap_live_*` for production, `isnap_test_*` for sandbox.

byod.description: True when the customer owns the underlying hardware (BYOD billing tiers). BYOD lines expose the full line-health surface (offline/degraded events, GET /v1/lines/{id}/health). Rental lines (false) only emit durable, actionable events to keep customers out of transient infrastructure noise they cannot act on.

checkout_url.description: Hosted Stripe Checkout URL — redirect the customer here.

device_count.description: Number of BYOD slots to purchase. Each slot pairs to one device.

billing_cycle.description: Stripe price cadence. Annual is 10x monthly (2 months free).

WebhookEventName.description: A concrete event type (e.g. `message.received`), a family wildcard (`line.*`), or the catch-all `*`.

size_bytes.description: Attachment size in bytes. Hard cap 5 GB (R2 single-PUT ceiling); oversize requests are rejected with HTTP 413 `attachment_exceeds_storage_limit`. Sizes above 100 MB succeed but carry a `large_attachment_may_delay_delivery` warning.

expires_at.description: Activation code expiry — 5 minutes from issue.

bridge_download_url.description: Presigned R2 GET for the bridge installer (.dmg or .apk). 5-minute TTL.

setup_instructions_url.description: Deep link to the platform-specific BYOD setup docs.

device_type.description: BYOD device platform. macos_byod runs the iMessage bridge on a customer-owned Mac; android_byod runs the Android bridge on a customer-owned phone.

device_name.description: Customer-chosen friendly name surfaced in the dashboard.

attachments.description: Ordered list of `att_<base62>` attachment publicIds. Mint each ID via `POST /v1/attachments` and upload the bytes to the returned signed URL before referencing the ID here. Up to 10 attachments per message and 100 MB per attachment. Per-channel total budgets at delivery time: iMessage ~100 MB, RCS ~10 MB, SMS ~1 MB — the device picks the transport at send time and degrades to a lower-cap channel only when iMessage is unavailable.
